items.question: Under what condition can one remain uncut even when in the act of being cut, according to the focus of mind?
premises: Cutting may be underway upon a person at a given time.
A mind fixed upon that object follows a distinct orientation.
That orientation can prevent the act of cutting from taking effect.
items.inference: When the mind is fixed upon that object, the one being cut is not cut, just as the stated comparison holds.
uncertainties: The precise scope of 'that' remains determined by immediate context.
items.plain_english: Just as one whose mind is fixed on that object is not cut even while being cut, so too the effect does not take hold in that state.
